title: M3-AD: Reflection-aware Multi-modal, Multi-category, and Multi-dimensional Benchmark and Framework for Industrial Anomaly Detection
claim: A reward-trained monitor lets a model reflect on and revise its unreliable first answer, yielding better detection and localization than baselines.
layout: 4 top panels left-to-right with arrows, bottom strip of 3 result panels
description: The figure has two tiers. The top tier has four dashed rounded panels connected by large hollow arrows: Base Model, RA-Monitor, Reflection and Revision. Base Model shows a screw image with a question and an overconfident answer that mislabels the defect as a crack, plus a dizzy emoji. RA-Monitor shows the M3-AD-FT thinking mode feeding a warm-start robot. Three reward items sit below it: consistency, accuracy and reflection, with an UPDATE arrow. Reflection shows a zoomed defect crop, a 'crack or damage?' query, a corrected 'scrape' label, and a thinking emoji. Revision shows the revised text, the screw with a bounding box, and a happy emoji. The bottom tier has three panels: a pie chart of the M3-AD dataset composition (38.4K samples), a bar chart of detection accuracy and balance, and a bar chart of localization with medals for 'Ours'. Red marks the proposed models.
caption: M3-AD enables self-correction of unreliable initial predictions through a reflection-aware mechanism, significantly improving anomaly type recognition and spatial localization in industrial anomaly detection compared to base models.
abstract: Although multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced industrial anomaly detection toward a zero-shot paradigm, they still tend to produce high-confidence yet unreliable decisions in fine-grained and structurally complex industrial scenarios, and lack effective self-corrective mechanisms. To address this issue, we propose M3-AD, a unified reflection-aware multimodal framework for industrial anomaly detection. M3-AD comprises two complementary data resources: M3-AD-FT, designed for reflection-aligned fine-tuning, and M3-AD-Bench, designed for systematic cross-category evaluation, together providing a foundation for reflection-aware learning and reliability assessment. Building upon this foundation, we propose RA-Monitor, which models reflection as a learnable decision revision process and guides models to perform controlled self-correction when initial judgments are unreliable, thereby improving decision robustness. Extensive experiments conducted on M3-AD-Bench demonstrate that RA-Monitor outperforms multiple open-source and commercial MLLMs in zero-shot anomaly detection and anomaly analysis tasks. Code will be released at https://github.com/Yanhui-Lee/M3-AD.
